source.title: Unsupervised label noise modeling and loss correction
source.authors: Eric Arazo; Diego Ortego; Paul Albert; N. O'Connor; Kevin McGuinness

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present. Some figure results are supplied only as plots.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures clean and noisy sample losses over training and reports that clean samples are learned before noisy ones, bearing directly on V6. It does not reproduce the original random-label experiment or report the training and test error measures required by V1.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports the study's own cross-entropy loss trajectories on CIFAR-10 with 80% label noise, for standard cross-entropy and the proposed objective. Other reported accuracy tables measure validation accuracy under noisy labels, not training error on completely random labels or test error at chance. Claims about prior studies in the introduction and related work are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own clean-versus-noisy loss trajectories, testing V6. Its standard cross-entropy validation results across corruption levels also test the degradation component of V4, although perfect training fit and complete randomization are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The principal conclusion is that an unsupervised beta mixture of sample losses enables dynamic bootstrapping, combined with mixup, to improve robustness to label noise without a clean training subset. Clean-before-noisy learning motivates the method. Results extend to TinyImageNet, with limitations on Clothing1M.
record.recipe_differences: This study evaluates loss correction and mixup for training with corrupted labels; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss behavior is conditioned on CIFAR-10 with 80% label noise and the training objective. In Clothing1M, the authors say structured noise and a small learning rate limit their noise model.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed objective prevents noisy-label fitting while retaining useful learning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss correction combined with mixup can mitigate noisy-label memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: On Clothing1M, one epoch of pretrained-network fine-tuning easily fits label noise and limits the noise model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rapid fitting of structured label noise can undermine loss-based noise identification during fine-tuning; no clean-versus-noisy learning order is established.

record.problems: Figure 1 supplies loss trajectories only as plots, without numeric values. The relevant loss-ordering result is limited to CIFAR-10 at 80% label noise; no direct training-error or test-error measurements for the claim's random-label setting are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Validation-accuracy tables across corruption levels do not measure the training fit and chance-level test error required by V1 or V4.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely randomized labels, chance-level test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
The training-time factor relative to true labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Perfect training fit throughout the corruption sweep, the completely randomized endpoint, and the full continuous degradation curve.
Whether the specified regularizers prevent complete random-label fitting, and generalization after removing them.
Direct measurement of shared-pattern learning, and comparable temporal ordering across architectures, datasets, and structured-noise conditions.

missing.what: Early clean/noisy loss distributions under standard cross-entropy at 50% corruption. Record the qualitative separation without inventing numerical distribution values.
missing.locator: Figure 2 and Section 3.1; CIFAR-10, epoch 10, learning rate 0.1

missing.what: Standard cross-entropy final validation accuracies at 0%, 20%, 50%, and 80% corruption: Table 1 CIFAR-10: 93.7%, 81.8%, 55.9%, 25.3%; Table 2 CIFAR-10: 94.6%, 82.9%, 58.4%, 26.3%; Table 2 CIFAR-100: 75.9%, 62.0%, 37.7%, 8.9%. Preserve the distinct 120-epoch and 300-epoch schedules. These results were declared omitted, but the exclusion incorrectly treats V4's unmeasured training-fit component as excluding its measured degradation component.

record.verdict_notes: Random replacement draws from all classes, so the nominal corruption fraction includes labels that happen to remain correct. Numerical Figure 1 trajectories are unavailable in the supplied text; the qualitative V6 verdict rests on the authors' explicit description. The record's declared omission of validation tables does not eliminate their relevance to V4's degradation component.

versions.untested_parts: No reported training-error result for completely random labels, test error at chance, or comparison showing these outcomes without changes to architecture or training hyperparameters.
No training-time comparison between fitting random labels and true labels, or measured convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
No experiments on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The study reports validation accuracy at several label-noise levels, but does not report perfect training fit across those levels or test error rising steadily toward chance.
No random-label experiments testing whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting, and no removal experiments on generalization.

Tests clean and noisy sample loss trajectories on CIFAR-10 with 80% label noise; does not compare separate learning dynamics across other corruption rates or report a direct measure of patterns shared by real data.
